source_title: 'Ramayana' advance booking: Ranbir starrer crosses Rs 17 cr in India, nears USD 3 mn overseas
source_excerpt: Nitesh Tiwariâs mythological epic âRamayana: Part 1â is gathering strong pace in advance bookings ahead of its November 5 release. Overseas markets are leading the charge, while domestic sales are picking up after a delayed rollout. Headlined by Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, the film is drawing steady interest from audiences at home and abroad.India advance sales cross Rs 17 croreAccording to trade website Sacnilk, the film has earned Rs 17.14 crore in advance sales in India as of 11 am on October 30. After removing blocked seats, the figure stands at Rs 14.29 crore. Around 3.34 lakh tickets have been sold across the country, which drops to 2.75 lakh without blocked seats. Between 6 am and 11 am, the film added Rs 7.25 lakh to its tally.Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash takes on the role of Ravana. The film has built this momentum despite a limited booking rollout over the last few days.Overseas pre-sales near USD 3 millionInternational advance bookings are closing in on USD 3 million, which is roughly Rs 28 crore. North America remains the biggest contributor, bringing in close to USD 1.9 million, which is nearly three-fourths of the overseas total. The UK and Ireland have added around USD 268,000, while Australia and New Zealand have contributed about USD 248,000. Other markets make up the rest.Paid previews planned for November 4 have also boosted the North American numbers. With six days still left for the release, overseas sales could grow further.Multiplex chain calls response to 'Ramayana' 'very encouraging'"The response to 'Ramayana' has been very encouraging, with advance bookings crossing 2.5 lakh tickets across the PVR INOX circuit. The filmâs opening during a six-day festive window is well timed, as this is traditionally a period when families come together and cinema becomes a natural part of the celebrations. Given the storyâs deep cultural connect and appeal across generations, we believe Ramayana has the potential to draw audiences in large numbers and contribute meaningfully to the festive box office," shared Sanjeev Kumar Bijli, Executive Director, PVR INOX Limited.Distribution deadlock delays booking rolloutThe domestic booking window was held up because distributors and exhibitors could not agree on revenue-sharing terms. The disagreement was about how much of the box office earnings distributors would receive in the opening weeks.As per the report, distributors put forward two proposals. The first was a three-week structure, with 60 per cent for the distributor in Week 1, 50 per cent in Week 2 and 40 per cent in Week 3. The second asked for a flat 55 per cent share for the first 11 days in a row, after which the usual industry slabs would apply.The makers reportedly felt the scale of the project justified better terms. The combined budget of both parts is estimated at around Rs 4,000 crore, and the team wanted a bigger share of earnings during the crucial opening period.Exhibitors, on the other hand, pointed to operating costs and the risk of giving a large number of screens to one film while agreeing to higher distributor shares. There was also worry that such terms could set a precedent for future big-budget releases.Bookings open as talks easeThe deadlock has reportedly eased, and bookings have started at cinemas where distribution terms are settled. More theatres are expected to open sales as agreements are reached, with the remaining listings likely to go live by 7 pm on October 30. This wider rollout could give Indiaâs advance sales another push in the coming days.Hindi markets are currently leading ticket sales, while the Kannada and Telugu versions are also gaining ground. Tamil and Malayalam listings are expected to grow as the rollout continues.Cast and crew of âRamayana: Part 1âApart from the three leads, the ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Arun Govil as King Dasharatha. Lara Dutta plays Kaikeyi, Indira Krishnan is Kaushalya, Kajal Aggarwal is Mandodari, and Rakul Preet Singh appears as Surpanakha. Vivek Oberoi is Vidyutjihva, Shobana is Kaikasi, Sheeba Chaddha is Manthara, and Saurabh Sachdeva is Mareech. Kunal Kapoor plays Lord Indra, Faisal Malik is Kumbhkarna, and Raghav Juyal is Meghnad, also known as Indrajit.Namit Malhotra has produced the film, with music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. âRamayana: Part 1â is set to release in theatres on November 5, 2026.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
